recognize_zh: 箭頭所指的紅血球內，各有一顆單一、小而圓、深紫色的點狀包涵體，通常靠近細胞邊緣，就是 Howell-Jolly body。背景紅血球大小形狀不一，可見棘狀細胞、碎片與標靶樣細胞，提示脾功能低下或其他紅血球生成異常。
features: Single, small (about 1 µm), round, dense dark purple inclusion within several red cells (arrows), often eccentric
One inclusion per cell, sharply defined and uniform, unlike fine diffuse stippling
Marked anisopoikilocytosis with echinocytes/acanthocyte-like cells, irregular fragments and target-like cells
Scattered platelets in the background; no nucleated cells in this field
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows marked anisopoikilocytosis with crenated and spiculated red cells, irregular red cell fragments and occasional target-like forms. Several red cells contain a single small, round, dense basophilic inclusion, typically located near the cell periphery, consistent with Howell-Jolly bodies. Platelets are present and nucleated red cells are not seen in this field. Findings are consistent with Howell-Jolly bodies, suggesting hyposplenism/asplenia or dyserythropoiesis; correlation with splenic status is recommended.

ddx.vs: Pappenheimer bodies are multiple, smaller, irregular granules clustered at the cell periphery and are iron positive on Prussian blue, whereas Howell-Jolly bodies are single, round, larger DNA remnants.
Basophilic stippling consists of numerous fine or coarse dots distributed throughout the cell, not a single discrete round body.
An overlying platelet is larger, shows granular texture with a pale halo and lies in a different focal plane.
Parasites show a blue cytoplasmic ring with a red chromatin dot rather than a solid dense purple sphere.
